exact_items: Plans/Prompt_Pipeline.md is mostly aligned on field names, but it still carries stale scope wording:
run envelope still says tier
persona_override_owner_id still allows tier_id
run-envelope and override-owner wording stop using tier / tier_id as canonical scope labels.
Plans/Contracts_V0.md still names run.tier_started / run.tier_completed and run.persona_stage_changed; its examples still include tier_id / tier_type
Plans/storage-plan.md still centers tier_id; several runtime events are still defined as tier-boundary or tier-start records; tier_runtime_record is still named as canonical
The event-family layer is still one of the last upstream carriers of stale execution semantics.

Plans/storage-plan.md still teaches canonical event families such as: run.tier_started, run.tier_completed, run.verification_result, run.persona_stage_changed, run.qa_cycle_started, run.qa_cycle_completed
Plans/human-in-the-loop.md is still explicitly built around: request_id, tier_id, tier_type, request_kind = tier_boundary_approval

Downstream consumers mirror that split: cmd.graph.approve_hitl and cmd.graph.deny_hitl still take request_id; Run_Graph_View.md still exposes hitl_request_id; Orchestrator_Page.md still describes HITL requests as hitl.* events keyed by request_id
The blocked/runtime lineage work already moved toward: node.blocked, blocked_sequence, ordered allowed_action_ids[]
